verdict.root_cause: Not established. Every one of the four available dispatches was spent on change-history lookups (frontend, productcatalogservice, paymentservice, recommendationservice), and all four returned empty for the 11:36:45–11:51:45 window [tr_ba86682f2804, tr_fd59daaeec9c, tr_dcfcb81e06f4, tr_eecdb95b450a]. That negative result is real but narrow: it says no deploy, config edit, flag flip, or rollback was recorded against those four services inside a 15-minute window, and nothing more. No metric, log, trace, dependency, or saturation evidence was ever collected, and the remaining ten alerting services (checkoutservice, cartservice, currencyservice, emailservice, accountingservice, frauddetectionservice, quoteservice, shippingservice, adservice-tier, loadgenerator) were never queried at all. The observed shape — onset at frontend and loadgenerator at 11:46:45, checkoutservice fifteen seconds later, then a broad fan-out to eight more services within a minute — is consistent with a single failing backend on the checkout path propagating outward, but the evidence in hand cannot name that backend or say whether it is failing by exhaustion, by waiting on a slow dependency, by running a wrong artifact, or on a wrong configuration value. Assigning a mechanism here would be a guess dressed as a finding.
verdict.reasoning: The four findings are mutually consistent and individually high-confidence, but they are all the same kind of evidence — an absence in one log, over one window, for four of fourteen implicated services. An empty change log narrows the candidate set for those four services only, and the specialists themselves flag the limit: tr_ba86682f2804 notes that 45 of the requested 60 pre-incident minutes were never examined, so a change that landed before 11:36:45 and detonated later remains entirely unexcluded. Nothing in the collected evidence speaks to the mechanism the taxonomy asks about. There is no memory, CPU, connection-pool, or thread-pool measurement, so resource_exhaustion is untested. There is no latency or dependency-call data, so dependency_latency is untested. There is no image, digest, or version inspection and no pod-state evidence, so bad_deploy is untested for every service including the ten never queried. bad_config is likewise untested, and the empty change logs do not rule it out — a wrong value that predates the window would leave no in-window record. The past incidents are suggestive rather than probative: cart-bad-image-tag opened with the same alert triple (frontend, loadgenerator, checkoutservice) and fanned out to seven more services, which loosely matches the shape here, but shape similarity is not a diagnosis, and cartservice was never one of the four services queried in this investigation. Choosing bad_deploy on that resemblance would be importing last time's answer. remediation_class is 'none' not because no action is warranted but because no evidence identifies an action that would resolve this; the correct next step is investigation, not a fix.
open_questions: What is failing on the checkout path? checkoutservice alerted at 11:47:00, fifteen seconds after frontend, and cartservice, currencyservice, emailservice, frauddetectionservice, quoteservice, shippingservice, and accountingservice all alerted at 11:47:45 — none of these eight were queried for changes, health, or dependency state.

Did a change land between 10:46:45 and 11:36:45? The change query covered only the final 15 minutes of the intended 60-minute lookback [tr_ba86682f2804], leaving a 45-minute pre-incident gap in which a deploy or config push could have occurred.
Which service is the propagation origin? Triage names frontend as the start point but crossed 5 unmeasured edges, so the true upstream failure may sit behind an edge that was never measured.
Is any service showing resource saturation (OOM kills, restart counts, pool exhaustion)? No metric or pod-state evidence was gathered for any service.
Are latencies elevated anywhere, and if so at which hop? No trace or latency data was collected, so dependency_latency can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
Do the running artifacts match the intended versions? No image tag, digest, or replica-readiness check was performed on any of the fourteen services.

Is the loadgenerator signal independent, or does it merely restate frontend's failure as in the ad-memory-squeeze precedent? Request-volume data would settle whether an unusual load pattern contributed.
